statement: The sharp maximum number of real rational cubics through eight general real points is twelve. All twelve are real exactly when the pencil contains two real cubics with solitary double points.

answer.text: The maximum number of real rational cubics through eight generic real points is twelve, so total reality occurs. All twelve are real precisely when the pencil has two real cubics with solitary double points.

source.location: Proposition 4.7.3 and preceding “Digression: real rational curves”, printed p.50

notes:
Although the article is broadly a survey, this association records its concrete proved proposition and explicit occurrence statement. Counts concern real curves, not a claim about a full chamber classification; singular/nongeneric point configurations are excluded.
